stem: Adeel looks at the diagram. Endpoints $X$ and $Y$ are marked. Points $P$ and $Q$ each lie at the same distance from $X$ as from $Y$. Line $n$ is drawn through $P$ and $Q$, and it meets $XY$ at $M$ with a right-angle mark.

options.text: Line $n$ is the perpendicular bisector of segment $XY$.
Equal distances from $X$ and $Y$ appear only after line $n$ is already drawn.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Points $P$ and $Q$ are each the same distance from $X$ as from $Y$, so the line through them is the perpendicular bisector of $XY$.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal-distance points from the endpoints determine the perpendicular bisector. Calling n the segment XY substitutes the wrong object; saying equal distances follow the line reverses the construction.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle rods as segment XY with equal-distance points P,Q and perpendicular bisector n through midpoint M.
